title: Groq vs Google Gemini Free Tier: Which Should You Use?
description: Groq vs Gemini free tier in 2026: models, rate limits, context, speed, multimodal and data policy, checked against the official docs.
author: freellm.site
content:
**Pick Groq** if you want the fastest responses from open-weight models like GPT-OSS 120B and Qwen 3.8 27B, and you don't want your free-tier prompts used to train anyone's models. **Pick Google Gemini** if you need a 1M-token context window, native image/audio/video/PDF input, or more daily headroom on current Gemini 3.x Flash models, and you're fine with Google using free-tier content to improve its products.

Neither asks for a credit card, and both expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so the best answer for most projects is to use both. The sections below show how to divide the work between them.

*All figures below were checked against Groq's and Google's official documentation on 29 September 2026. Free tiers change often, so confirm your own limits in the [Groq console](https://console.groq.com/settings/limits) and [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/) before you depend on them.*

## Groq vs Gemini free tier at a glance

| | [Groq](/providers/groq/) (Free plan) | [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) (Free tier) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free chat models now | `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` | `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, Gemma 4 |
| Other free models | Whisper Large v3 / v3 Turbo (speech-to-text), Orpheus TTS, Llama Prompt Guard 2 | Gemini Embedding 2, Live/Transcribe audio models, Flash TTS |
| RPM | 30 (chat models) | Per model and per project, shown in AI Studio |
| RPD | 1,000 (chat models) | Per model, shown in AI Studio; resets at midnight Pacific |
| TPM / TPD | 8K TPM / 200K TPD | Per model, shown in AI Studio |
| Context window | 131,072 tokens | 1,048,576 input tokens (65,536 output) |
| Speed (published) | ~500 tok/s (GPT-OSS 120B), ~1,000 tok/s (GPT-OSS 20B), ~450 tok/s (Qwen 3.8 27B) | Not published |
| Multimodal input | Images (Qwen 3.8 27B only, max 3 per request) + audio via Whisper | Text, image, video, audio and PDF on all Flash models |
| Credit card | No | No |
| Free-tier data use | Not retained by default; Zero Data Retention available to all | Content used to improve Google products; human reviewers may read it |
| OpenAI-compatible | Yes: `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | Yes (beta): `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/` |

Sources: [Groq rate limits](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits), [Groq models](https://console.groq.com/docs/models), [Groq vision](https://console.groq.com/docs/vision), [Groq data policy](https://console.groq.com/docs/your-data), [Gemini pricing](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing), [Gemini rate limits](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits), [Gemini 3.8 Flash model card](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.8-flash), [Gemini API terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms).

For a table that updates automatically, see our [Groq vs Google Gemini comparison page](/compare/groq-vs-google_gemini/).

## What changed in 2026

If you last looked at these two in 2025, three things have changed.

**Llama has left Groq's free plan.** `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` and `llama-3.1-8b-instant` still appear on Groq's [models page](https://console.groq.com/docs/models), but they're now labelled *Enterprise*, and they're no longer in the free-plan rate-limit table. On the free plan you now get OpenAI's open-weight GPT-OSS models and Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 27B. Tutorials that hard-code a Llama model ID on Groq will fail on a free key.

**Gemini 1.5 is gone, and 2.5 is being wound down.** The free lineup now runs from Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite to Gemini 3.8 Flash. Gemini 2.5 Pro, Flash and Flash-Lite are still priced as free, but Google's [model page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-2.5-pro) says access is now limited to people who have used them before, and it points new projects to 3.5 Flash-Lite or 3.8 Flash. The 2M-token context window that Gemini 1.5 Pro used to offer is also gone. Every current Gemini model accepts 1,048,576 input tokens.

**Gemini's free limits are no longer published.** Google's [rate-limits page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits) now points you to AI Studio for your live numbers. It says limits "depend on a variety of factors (such as your usage tier)", are applied per project rather than per API key, and are "not guaranteed". Treat any fixed "15 RPM / 1,500 RPD" figure you see elsewhere as out of date.

## Rate limits: what "free" buys you

Groq publishes exact free-plan numbers. Every current free chat model gets **30 RPM, 1,000 RPD, 8,000 TPM and 200,000 TPD**, applied at the organization level. The TPM cap is the one that catches people out. According to Groq's docs, you hit whichever limit you reach first, so a single 10K-token prompt goes over the 8K per-minute budget however few requests you send. In practice, Groq's free plan suits short and medium prompts. It won't let you use the full 131K window. Tokens served from Groq's prompt cache don't count toward your limits, so a repeated system prompt costs you less than it looks.

Gemini's free limits are set per model and per project, and you have to check them in AI Studio. The trade-off is a much larger per-request ceiling. You can send hundreds of thousands of tokens in a single call, which Groq's free TPM rules out. Limits are tighter on preview and experimental models, so use the stable IDs listed above.

Both APIs return HTTP 429 when you go over a limit. Groq also sends `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` and `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` headers on every response, so you can throttle before you hit the wall. For a side-by-side of every provider's limits, see [free LLM API rate limits compared](/blog/free-llm-api-rate-limits-compared/).

## Best choice by use case

### Chatbots and real-time assistants: Groq

For chat, latency is what users notice first. Groq publishes throughput for each model: about 1,000 tokens/s for GPT-OSS 20B and about 500 tokens/s for GPT-OSS 120B. At those speeds a typical reply streams out almost at once. Chat turns are short, so they sit comfortably within the 8K TPM limit, and 1,000 requests a day is plenty for a prototype, a Discord bot or an internal helpdesk.

Use Gemini for chat when the conversation needs grounding in a large knowledge base in one shot, or when users upload screenshots and PDFs. Our [customer support chatbot guide](/blog/free-llm-api-customer-support-chatbot/) walks through a full build.

### RAG and long documents: Gemini

This is where Gemini is strongest. A 1,048,576-token input window holds a whole codebase, a long contract or several hundred pages of a report. Every current Flash model also accepts PDF input directly, so you don't need a separate text-extraction step. For many "chat with this document" projects you can drop the vector database entirely and put the whole document in the prompt.

Groq still has a place in a classic RAG pipeline: retrieve 3 to 5 short chunks, keep the prompt under about 6K tokens, and let Groq write the answer quickly. For the retrieval side, Gemini Embedding 2 is free as well. See [free LLM APIs for RAG and embeddings](/blog/free-llm-api-for-rag-embeddings/) and our ranking of [free APIs with the largest context windows](/blog/free-llm-api-largest-context-window/).

### Coding: it depends on the task

For **fast inline help** (completing a function, explaining an error, writing a regex), Groq's speed wins. Qwen 3.8 27B is Groq's strongest free coding option. Groq lists 90.3% on LiveCodeBench v6 and 61.7% on SWE-bench Pro for it, and it supports tool use, JSON schema mode and adjustable reasoning. Its 16,384-token output cap is enough for most edits.

For **repo-scale work** (refactoring across many files, reviewing a large diff, planning a migration), Gemini 3.8 Flash is the better fit. Google describes it as "engineered for long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents", and its 1M-token input and 65,536-token output mean it can read the code and write the result in a single pass. More options are in [best free LLM APIs for coding](/blog/best-free-llm-apis-for-coding/), and editor setup is covered in [using free LLM APIs in Cursor and Claude Code](/blog/use-free-llm-api-cursor-claude-code/).

### Multimodal: Gemini, with one exception

Every current Gemini Flash model accepts **text, image, video, audio and PDF** in a single request. That covers OCR on invoices, summarising a meeting recording, pulling data from a chart, or answering questions about a video. Groq's free vision support comes from one model, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, which takes up to 3 images per request (20 MB max, 2,048 tokens per image) and returns text. Groq has no video input.

The exception is **speech-to-text**. Groq's free Whisper Large v3 and v3 Turbo are fast, but the free quota is small: 20 RPM, 2,000 RPD and 7,200 audio seconds per hour, which works out to about two hours of audio an hour. For short voice notes or a voice-bot front end, Groq Whisper is hard to beat. Longer recordings will hit that hourly limit quickly.

### Prototyping at scale: use both, and read the data policy first

Once you're running evals, batch-labelling data or hammering an agent loop, you'll run into Groq's 200K TPD. Gemini's per-project limits usually give you more room on cheap models like `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, which Google positions for "high-volume agentic workflows, simple data extraction". Spread the load across providers rather than creating extra accounts to get around limits. Groq's [data policy](https://console.groq.com/docs/your-data) specifically mentions investigating "rate-limit circumvention".

**Data policy matters more than any benchmark here.** Gemini's [terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms) say that on unpaid quota Google uses your prompts and responses "to provide, improve, and develop Google products", and that "human reviewers may read, annotate, and process your API input and output". Google's advice is blunt: do not submit sensitive, confidential or personal information. The same terms say that apps serving users in the **EEA, Switzerland or the UK** must use Gemini's paid tier.

Groq takes the opposite default. It doesn't retain inference inputs or outputs, except for short-term logs of up to 30 days kept for reliability or abuse checks. Any account can switch those logs off by enabling Zero Data Retention in Data Controls. If you're prototyping with real customer data, that difference alone can settle the choice.

## Code: one client, two providers

Both providers work with the official `openai` Python SDK. You only change `base_url`, `api_key` and `model`. The base URLs below come from [Groq's OpenAI compatibility doc](https://console.groq.com/docs/openai) and [Google's OpenAI compatibility doc](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai). Keys come from [console.groq.com/keys](https://console.groq.com/keys) and [aistudio.google.com/app/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey). Neither needs a card; see [how to get a free LLM API key without a credit card](/blog/how-to-get-free-llm-api-key-no-credit-card/).

**Groq:**

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

groq = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"],
)

resp = groq.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain rate limiting in two sentences."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

**Gemini:**

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

gemini = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",
    api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
)

resp = gemini.chat.completions.create(
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain rate limiting in two sentences."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

A few compatibility notes from the docs:

- **Groq** rejects `logprobs`, `logit_bias`, `top_logprobs` and `messages[].name` with a 400 error, and `n` must be 1.
- **Gemini's** OpenAI compatibility layer is still labelled beta. `reasoning_effort` maps to Gemini's thinking levels. Images go in as `image_url` content parts and audio as `input_audio`, in the same format OpenAI uses.

For more on the pattern, see our [OpenAI-compatible API guide](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/).

## When to use both

Groq and Gemini complement each other: Groq offers speed and privacy, Gemini offers context and modalities. Because both speak the same API, routing between them takes a few lines of code:

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI, RateLimitError

groq = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
              api_key=os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"])
gemini = OpenAI(base_url="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",
                api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])

def ask(messages, approx_tokens, has_media=False):
    # Long prompts and images/audio/PDF go straight to Gemini.
    if has_media or approx_tokens > 6000:
        return gemini.chat.completions.create(model="gemini-3.8-flash", messages=messages)
    try:
        return groq.chat.completions.create(model="openai/gpt-oss-120b", messages=messages)
    except RateLimitError:
        # Groq free plan hit 30 RPM / 8K TPM / 1K RPD: fall back.
        return gemini.chat.completions.create(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", messages=messages)
```

Common splits that work well:

- **Router pattern:** short, latency-sensitive turns go to Groq; anything over about 6K tokens or containing media goes to Gemini.
- **Two-stage pipeline:** Gemini reads the long document or video and writes a compact summary, then Groq handles fast follow-up chat over that summary.
- **Fallback pattern:** Groq first; on a 429, retry on Gemini. Your combined free throughput is roughly the sum of both quotas.
- **Privacy split:** anything containing personal or customer data goes only to Groq (with Zero Data Retention on); public or synthetic data can go to either.

If you want a third fast, no-card endpoint in the rotation, Cerebras and SambaNova slot in the same way. See [Groq vs Cerebras vs SambaNova](/blog/groq-vs-cerebras-vs-sambanova-free-tier/).

## The verdict

- **Speed, privacy, open-weight models, short prompts:** Groq (`openai/gpt-oss-120b` or `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`).
- **Long context, PDFs, images, audio, video, repo-scale coding:** Gemini (`gemini-3.8-flash`, or `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` for volume).
- **Anything serious:** both, behind one OpenAI client, with Groq as the fast path and Gemini as the long-context path and fallback.

See the live details on the [Groq](/providers/groq/) and [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) provider pages, or browse the [full directory](/) for alternatives.
